_comment: SHA-256 vectors for the hex formatting every gnomon hash is printed through.
Added when sha2 was taken from 0.10 to 0.11. That major swapped the digest
return type from generic_array::GenericArray to hybrid_array::Array, which
does NOT implement LowerHex -- so `format!("{:x}", hasher.finalize())` stopped
compiling and had to be replaced by an explicit encoder in three crates.
The DIGEST could not change (SHA-256 is SHA-256) but the ENCODING could, and
nothing pinned it: a hand-written encoder that drops a leading zero, or emits
uppercase, produces a wrong hash string from a correct digest. Every surface
hash, manifest sha256, audit chain link and patch pre/post image is that
string. `leading-zero-nibble` exists so the zero-padding is covered by data
Vectors computed with Python's hashlib, i.e. not by the implementation they
pin. digests are lowercase, zero-padded, exactly 64 hex characters.

vectors.name: pangram
vectors.input: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog
